iot.name: sites
iot.description:
List sorted site identifiers available in the asset registry.

    Returns:
        SitesResult: Distinct site identifiers, or `["MAIN"]` when the registry
        lists none.

iot.name: asset_ids
iot.description:
List asset identifiers registered at one site.

    Use `assets()` when registry metadata is also needed.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.

    Returns:
        AssetsResult: Sorted asset identifiers and their count.

iot.name: asset_detail
iot.description:
Return registry details for one asset.

    Includes identity, description, type, status, location, installation date,
    vintage, and installed-sensor count. Use `installed_sensors()` for names.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.

    Returns:
        AssetDetail: The available registry fields; optional values are null
        when absent.

iot.name: measured_sensors
iot.description:
List measurement fields observed in an asset's telemetry stream.

    Returns the sorted union across the full stream, excluding record metadata.
    Use `installed_sensors()` for assigned sensors, which may differ.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.

    Returns:
        SensorsResult: Observed measurement field names and their count.

iot.name: installed_sensors
iot.description:
List sensor names assigned to an asset in the registry.

    Use `measured_sensors()` for fields observed in telemetry; the two lists may
    differ.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.

    Returns:
        SensorsResult: Sensor names in registry order and their count.

iot.name: assets
iot.description:
List assets at one site with compact registry metadata.

    Use `asset_ids()` for identifiers only and `asset_detail()` for more fields
    about one asset.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        assettype: Optional exact, case-sensitive asset type filter, such as
            `PUMP` or `COMPRESSOR`.

    Returns:
        AssetsWithMetadataResult: Assets sorted by identifier, with description,
        type, vintage, and installed-sensor count.

iot.name: find_assets_by_sensors
iot.description:
Find site assets by installed or measured sensor names.

    Searches only assets registered at `site_name`. Duplicate queries are
    removed while preserving first occurrence order.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        sensors: Sensor names, or fragments when `substring` is true.
        match: `all` requires every query; `any` requires at least one.
        substring: Use case-insensitive fragment matching instead of exact,
            case-sensitive matching.
        source: `measured` searches observed fields; `installed` searches
            registry assignments. Defaults to `measured`.

    Returns:
        FindAssetsResult: Query settings and matching assets with the concrete
        sensor names found.

iot.name: stream_extent
iot.description:
Inspect the size and timestamp span of an asset's telemetry stream.

    Optionally filter by one measured sensor and a half-open ISO 8601 window:
    `start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. Sensor-filtered records count
    only when the field is present and non-null. Bounds and record timestamps
    must consistently include or omit timezone offsets; aware timestamps are
    compared by instant even when their offsets differ.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.
        sensor: Optional exact field name from `measured_sensors()`.
            Reserved metadata fields such as `asset_id` and `timestamp` are not
            valid sensor names.
        start: Optional inclusive ISO 8601 date or datetime lower bound.
        end: Optional exclusive ISO 8601 date or datetime upper bound.

    Returns:
        StreamExtentResult: Earliest and latest matching timestamps, record
        count, whether the count exceeds one 1000-record page, and average
        interval implied by the span and count.

iot.name: history
iot.description:
Return one chronological page of telemetry observations for an asset.

    Optional bounds form a half-open ISO 8601 window. Use `sensors` to project
    exact measured fields; omit it to return all measured fields present in each
    row. Every row includes `asset_id` and `timestamp` and excludes other record
    metadata.

    Leave `cursor` unset for the first page. When `has_more` is true, repeat the
    same query with `next_cursor`. Cursors are opaque and query-bound. Timestamp
    offset rules match `stream_extent()`.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.
        start: Optional inclusive ISO 8601 lower bound.
        end: Optional exclusive ISO 8601 upper bound.
        sensors: Optional non-empty list of exact measured field names. Duplicate
            names are removed while preserving order.
        limit: Maximum observations in this page, from 1 to 1000.
        cursor: Opaque `next_cursor` from the previous page of the same query.

    Returns:
        HistoryResult: Projected observations, returned count, echoed bounds,
        and cursor fields for the next page.

iot.name: latest_reading
iot.description:
Return the newest telemetry observation for an asset.

    Omit `sensor` for all measured fields in the newest record. When a sensor is
    provided, returns the newest record where that field is present and non-null.
    Records are compared by parsed timestamp using the `stream_extent()` rules.

    `age_seconds` is the difference between the current UTC time and the reading
    timestamp. Offset-free timestamps are interpreted as UTC; a negative value
    indicates a timestamp in the future.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.
        sensor: Optional exact field name from `measured_sensors()`. Reserved
            metadata fields are not valid sensor names.

    Returns:
        LatestReadingResult: Selected timestamp, values, and age in seconds.

iot.name: sensor_coverage
iot.description:
Summarize non-null observation coverage for every measured sensor.

    Scans the full timestamped stream. `non_null_count` includes present,
    non-null values of any type. Fields observed only with null values have zero
    count and null bounds. Timestamp offset rules match `stream_extent()`.

    Args:
        site_name: Exact site id to query, such as `MAIN`. Use `sites()` to
            discover valid site ids.
        asset_id: Exact asset id from `asset_ids()`, such as `Chiller 6`.

    Returns:
        SensorCoverageResult: Timestamped records scanned and per-sensor counts
        and chronological bounds, sorted by field name.

fmsr.name: get_failure_modes
fmsr.description:
READ the known failure modes for an asset class.

    Args:
        asset_class: Asset class to look up, such as "pump". Case, whitespace,
            digits, underscores, and hyphens are normalized before querying.

wo.name: list_workorders
wo.description:
List work orders with optional filters (site, status, asset, priority, dates).
    status accepts OPEN / APPROVED_PENDING; page_size=0 returns all matches in one call.

wo.name: get_workorder
wo.description: Get a single work order by number and site.

wo.name: get_workorder_tasks
wo.description: List the child tasks of a parent work order.

wo.name: get_workorder_costs
wo.description: Actual labor/material/service/tool cost breakdown for a work order.

wo.name: get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned
wo.description: Estimated vs actual hours and cost variance for a work order.

wo.name: get_workorder_kpis
wo.description: Site KPIs: totals, backlog, overdue, avg completion, priority/asset breakdowns.

wo.name: get_schedule_calendar
wo.description: Scheduled (non-terminal) work orders in a date window, bucketed by day.

wo.name: get_my_assigned_workorders
wo.description: Work orders assigned to a given technician (labor code).

wo.name: get_failure_codes
wo.description:
Read the FCC failure-code reference catalog from CouchDB.

    Omit ``code`` to list all available failure codes, or pass an exact code
    such as ``FC001``. Matching is case-insensitive and CouchDB metadata is not
    returned.

wo.name: generate_work_order
wo.description: Create a work order (status WAPPR). Attach aob_source provenance (agent/trigger/evidence).

task.name: get_asset_profile
task.description: The asset profile: the asset with its type, description and site, components with their condition levels and healthy level, sensor groups with their channels and the served statistics, prices, durations, downtime rates, budget, horizon, step cap, the parameters of the schedule, hazard, emergency, dependency, priority, fix history and failure rules, the clock mode with the seconds per cycle, the seconds of thinking per cycle and the clock rules, the tool table and the normal ranges of the channel means. Free, takes no time.

task.name: get_current_time
task.description: Get the current time without moving the clock: the cycle, the horizon, the budget left, the seconds of wall clock time that one cycle stands for and the seconds of thinking that make one cycle. In the generation_time clock mode the seconds between your calls, and in the generated_tokens clock mode the seconds_per_token of every token you generate between them, add up, and every full think_seconds_per_cycle of them moves the clock one cycle before your next call runs. Free, takes no time. Like every answer of this server, it also lists the notifications since the previous call.

task.name: wait_for_notification
task.description: Wait for a specified number of cycles or until the next notification is received, whichever comes first, and return what ended the wait. The rig runs while it waits, so downtime accrues. Use it only when there are no other tasks to perform, for example while work orders are open. timeout is the largest number of cycles to wait, the cycles left before the horizon when it is left empty.

task.name: summarize_changes_since
task.description: The changes since a past cycle: the cycles elapsed, the channel means of the sensor groups already read in this episode that left their normal range, with the first such cycle, and the work orders closed since then. Free, takes no time.

task.name: submit_diagnosis
task.description: Submit the diagnosis: one condition level for each of the four components, with the comma separated evidence identifiers behind it (possibly empty). Accepted once per episode and never after a declaration of insufficient evidence. Free.

task.name: declare_insufficient_evidence
task.description: Declare that the evidence cannot separate the remaining candidates and name the reading that would (a sensor group and a number of cycles), with the comma separated evidence identifiers behind it. It must cite at least one reading already read, and a declaration that cites none is scored as a failure. Accepted once per episode and never after a diagnosis; work orders stay allowed afterward. Free.

task.name: finish
task.description: End the episode with a summary of what was found and done. On a row with a clock the rig then runs until the open work orders close, and the episode is scored after the last close. Free. A component that an emergency order still holds when the episode ends is scored at the level it had before that order.

causal_diagnosis.name: get_episode_evidence
causal_diagnosis.description: The sensor readings released so far as evidence items, each with an evidence ID, the cycle it was read at, the value, its unit, the public normal range of the channel mean and an anomaly score against the healthy recordings. sensor_group is all, tier1, tier2, tier3, a channel such as CE or its field name such as CE_CoolingEfficiency_percent_1Hz. Reads released values only; it never reads the rig.

causal_diagnosis.name: rank_root_causes
causal_diagnosis.description: Rank every level combination of the asset as the state of the rig now, by a belief that replays the released evidence from the start: a uniform prior times the released fix history, the public rule cards applied for every cycle that passed (closed work orders take only when the components they depend on are healthy), and every reading weighed by the interventional effect model. Returns the mass of the top combinations, the fault probability of every component now, the effective number of hypotheses and the cycle of the belief, and the decision whether to read first, read_first: true exactly when the rule of the server names one read of the recorded cycles before a diagnosis, through the sensor group that can still show the most summaries and, where readings have prices, that the budget pays beside the repair of every component, with that read as the separating test and the expected saving of the best single reading beside it. elimination gives, for every sensor group, the information gain of one cycle of it, the expected drop of the log of the effective number of hypotheses, and that gain per unit cost, which ranks the reads, with the expected number of hypotheses the cycle eliminates, its one step edge cutting score over repair plan classes (ec2, after the EC2 objective of Golovin, Krause and Ray, not their algorithm) and both per unit cost reported beside them, the cost being the test cost where reads, parts, repairs or visits cost money, else one call, and read_batch holds the reads of the rule in order, that one read where the sensor groups are nested, with left_to_read, the recorded cycles the row can still serve each group. The result also carries advice, the step that the scoring of the episode favors before a diagnosis: that read, else the diagnosis of the first candidate with one work order per faulty component. The details summary and full add e10_rule, the earlier rule with the margin, the cap, none unless the launch names one, and the reserve the server was launched with: read_first when the best single reading lowers the expected cost below acting now by more than the margin times its cost, that reading as its separating test, and its read_batch, the reads best first by gain per unit cost whose choice no outcome of the reads before them could change. top_k is the number of combinations to return, 5 unless the caller names more, with no maximum: the first top_k with positive probability by probability, ties by the combination in component order, and more_candidates gives how many combinations with positive probability the reply leaves out and their summed probability; set_masses gives, per faulty set with positive probability, the probability summed over every combination of that set, returned or not. Each distinct faulty set among the returned combinations also comes with a troubleshooting plan, one per set: the sensor group that would confirm or refute the set and by how much, the repair plan of the set as one technician visit with one visit charge, its lead time, the repairs in priority order, their dependencies, the cycles to a restored rig and the prediction ID every work order of the plan cites, the predicted recovery probability after that plan, and the predicted expected loss and cost to a restored state of acting on it now against testing it first. branch_detail is compact (the default: the plans of summary, without e10_rule, the attribution, the level probabilities, the stability, the Monte Carlo settings and the edge cutting scores, and with one assumption text), summary (adds e10_rule, the channels each component explains, the stability of the top component under resampling, the edge cutting scores and every assumption text) or full (summary with the predicted summaries after each plan and the separation of every sensor group).

causal_diagnosis.name: estimate_intervention_effect
causal_diagnosis.description: Predict what an action would do before it is taken: the probability that it addresses a fault, the probability that the rig is restored at the first reading after it, with the lead time, the repair downtime, the dependencies of the component and the rule cards acting meanwhile, its price with one visit charge, its duration, and the predicted summaries of that reading, those of the predicted combination, the most probable after the action, which the message names with its mass, with the intervals of the leave one block out conformal calibration at the declared error level. action is replace:<component> such as replace:cooler, a standard order, or monitor for one more cycle without a repair. Returns a prediction ID to cite in the work order and to pass to verify_outcome.

causal_diagnosis.name: verify_outcome
causal_diagnosis.description: Compare a stored prediction with the first reading after the work order closed: the largest standardized deviation over the channels read against the predicted combination, the most probable after the action, which the result names with its mass, its conformal p value and the verdict at the declared error level, which over a calibration block drawn at random and a cycle drawn in it finds a reading inconsistent at a rate of at most that level and promises no rate for one named combination, and the mass of the healthy combination in the belief now against the predicted recovery. prediction_id is the ID that estimate_intervention_effect returned, such as pred/1.
